kitDescription: Neon: Blue Ocean is a Water machine-gun attacker whose burst swaps her weapon for 7 seconds to a 33%-of-ATK gun, and while firing at a Fire-Code enemy each of those shots also lands an extra 11%-of-ATK hit. Her Skill 1 builds up a Damage-to-Parts buff each time she uses her burst (12.4% per tier, 20 seconds, cumulative to three tiers), which does nothing against a partless boss. Her Skill 2 builds an Elemental Advantage Attack Damage buff every time any ally takes the Burst Stage 3 slot (20.56% then 20.2% tiers, 10 seconds), so she ramps up over the fight specifically against bosses she has elemental advantage over. Everything she does is self-buffing; she brings no team utility, healing, or gauge tricks.

The refresh-vs-co-stack question is moot here (inert stat) but the driver kept the event-log pin for a future parts boss.

verdictRationale: No REAL-GOTCHAs: all four kit lines are FAITHFUL with their known unknowns (swap cadence ⚑1, cadence tuple ⚑2) documented with recipes and tiers. Convergence is real, not just same-model echo: the blind S5 suite runs GREEN against the shipped override after four banner-documented mechanics-only adaptations, and the one substantive disagreement chain resolved by evidence — all three blind roles independently derived stageEnter:3 for skill2, the driver flipped to match, and repo precedent (laplace-ultimate-hero, rei-ayanami) corroborates; that is three independent derivations plus prior cross-family validation, so the PROVE-IT-DIFFERENTLY bar is met and I stop there. The two divergences submitted for binding ruling both resolve for the driver: (1) the 11% Fire rider is window-scoped to the 7s swap (datamine ChangeWeapon duration_value + S2b + S5 against S6's self-admitted-uncertain whole-fight reading, the exact over-credit trap S2b predicted); (2) equal-value escalating steps refresh rather than co-stack per the official §11 rule, so skill2's live cap is 40.76 (elem mult 1.5076, pinned) — S2b's 60.96 expectation is an information-asymmetry recon note, not a finding. Discrimination holds on every load-bearing assertion (trigger keyings, window lengths, element gate, inertness pins all fail under their named nearest-wrong models). Residuals for the owner to spot-check, in order: (a) the refresh-vs-co-stack reading of 'each subsequent effect triggers all effects before it' — every agent here is the same model and all read §11 the same way; a single popup read of the element multiplier on a third stage-3 entry (1.5076 vs 1.7096) would settle it independently, and it is the only same-model-residual with real damage weight; (b) the ⚑1 swap-cadence measurement (recipe already written: isolated nbo-solo video, count rounds in one 7s window); (c) doc hygiene — game-mechanics.md §10 still says elemAdvantageDamagePct sits in Damage-Up while damage-calculation.md §1c (MEASURED, superseding) says element bucket; the driver followed the measured doc, and §10's stale sentence should be reconciled by the upkeep skill. Ship it.
